{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / The Associated Press)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.14 Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February
**Status:** 18 rules assessed — 8 compliant, 7 deviations, 3 missing

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement is structurally favourable to us on the commercial-freedom points: it imposes no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit, no liquidated damages or penalties, and no Vendor audit right against us. Kubient's indemnity in Section 10(a), read with the Section 9(b) warranties and the Section 11 procedure, sits at or above our preferred position and is materially better than fallback in that it carries no super-cap and no modification/combination exclusions. We do not redline any of these.

The gaps are concentrated in risk allocation and exit. Three rules have no usable clause at all: there is no IP or data-ownership article (our only licence is a revocable, non-transferable licence to the Auction Platform that is revoked on termination); there is no insurance provision, for a vendor that collects, manages and stores visitor data under Section 9(b)(iii); and there is no transition assistance or data-export obligation, Section 4(c) requiring only that Services cease and Confidential Information be returned or destroyed. Seven further clauses fail the fallback on material terms: Section 7 excludes consequential damages but imposes **no aggregate cap at all**; the assignment carve-out in paragraph (h) runs to Kubient as well as to us, with no bar on assignment to our competitor; the Section 2 licence does not reach our affiliates and cannot follow us into an M&A transaction; paragraph 4(a) gives us no convenience exit during the Initial Term while letting Kubient exit mid-renewal-term and offering us no non-renewal notice right inside the 60-day fallback ceiling; Section 14(a) picks Delaware law with New York courts while Section 8 mandates AAA arbitration, so the contract delivers no coherent forum; and the warranty package has no documentation-conformance period and no repair, replacement or refund remedy.

Our proposed redlines are surgical and, where the preferred position is a poor fit for a revenue-share deal with no prepaid fees, land deliberately at fallback.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section (as recorded) | Position / ask |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble | At or above preferred; uncapped and no combination exclusions. No redline (a fallback super-cap would weaken us). |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble | Insert fallback-level paragraph: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables (excluding the Auction Platform); Kubient's licence in our data limited to processing to provide the Services. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | Preamble | Add mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims; our payment obligations outside the cap. Existing mutual consequential-damages exclusion retained. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | Preamble | Make the affiliate/asset-purchaser/successor carve-out Customer-only; bar Kubient assignment to a Customer competitor. Balance of paragraph (h) unchanged. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Section 1 affirmatively disclaims exclusivity. No redline. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | Preamble | No LDs, penalties, early-termination or minimum fee payable by us. No redline. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble | Extend the Auction Platform licence to affiliates identified by written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor. Revocability left as-is (short of preferred, by design). |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us. No redline. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | Preamble | Confine the Initial Term lock-in to Kubient; give us an express 90-day convenience right with no timing restriction; anchor Kubient's no-cause right to the end of the then-current Term. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No Vendor audit right exists; better than preferred. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Preamble | New York law; exclusive merits resolution in New York County state and federal courts in place of mandatory AAA arbitration, retaining the temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out. |
| 12 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble | Insert new clause 14(j) at preferred limits: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber and privacy 5M where our data is handled, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN, best-terms or right-to-match running to Kubient. No redline. |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble | Pure revenue share; no minimum spend, take-or-pay or volume cap on us. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No restrictive covenant of any kind. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | Preamble | Add a 60-day Customer non-renewal notice right; 1-year renewal terms are acceptable and no price-uplift mechanic exists. |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble | Insert fallback clause: at least 90 days' transition assistance on expiry or termination and export of our data within 30 days. |
| 18 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | Preamble | Add 90-day software/deliverable documentation-conformance warranty, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replace or refund remedy. Section 13 disclaimer already preserves the express warranties. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Vendor insurance (Finding 12 — missing).** The Agreement has no insurance provision anywhere in the body and no exhibits are attached, yet Kubient collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor data under paragraph 9(b)(iii) and serves creatives onto our Properties. Absence of insurance for a vendor processing our data is walk-away territory for us; we require the new clause 14(j), with fallback limits available in negotiation.
2. **Non-renewal notice window (Finding 16 — deviation, at the boundary).** Our only exit is termination for any reason following the Initial Term on 90 days' notice, an effective 90-day window that exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling and sits at the walk-away boundary. We need the 60-day non-renewal right.
3. **Watch item — no liability cap (Finding 3).** Direct liability is currently unlimited on both sides. Not classified as walk-away, but we should not sign without the mutual cap and the Excluded Claims carve-outs; on a revenue-share deal a bare 12-months'-fees cap would be illusory, which is why we target the USD 1,000,000 floor.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations and three missing clauses, in the order of leverage: liability cap and insurance first, then IP/data ownership and transition assistance, then licence scope, assignment, termination/renewal, governing law and forum, and the warranty remedy.
2. **Resolve the forum conflict expressly.** Section 8's AAA arbitration mandate and Section 14(a)'s exclusive court jurisdiction contradict one another; our edit must conform both so the contract delivers a single forum. The Section 8 jury waiver, one-year limitation and the 14(d) fee-shifting reference are out of scope and stay untouched.
3. **Hold the line on the indemnity.** If Kubient reopens Section 10, do not trade our uncapped, exclusion-free indemnity for the playbook fallback structure. Optional upgrade asks only: name affiliates as indemnified parties and add a procure/modify/replace/refund ladder.
4. **Diligence the exhibits.** Commercial terms sit in the Exhibits and none is attached. Each executed Exhibit must be re-screened against MINCOMMIT (no minimum or shortfall), AUDIT (no usage or revenue-verification right; if one is sought, insert the preferred parameters — annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where possible, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access) and EXCLUSIVITY (Section 5's default that Kubient contracts with all Advertisers is overridable in an Exhibit).
5. **QC before circulation.** The termination-for-convenience proposal (Finding 9) was flagged as repaired in verification; re-read that draft language against paragraph 4(a), including the retained-fee sentence, before the redline goes out.
6. **Note for the internal file.** Sub-preferred points we are consciously not redlining: the licence remains revocable; affiliates are not named indemnified parties and there is no indemnity remedy ladder; AP's reciprocal 10(b) indemnity is broader than preferred; and the preferred 12-month software warranty and six-month/machine-readable/certified-deletion transition package remain upgrade asks only."}
